    "policy_clauses": [
     "§1 Contact ladder: on payment failure or day 1 overdue one courteous reminder; day 7 a reminder with payment link; day 14 a plan may be offered; day 21 final notice; day 30 HOLD for a human legal letter; never contact a customer more than once in 5 days or outside 08:00-18:00 customer time.",
     "§2 Instalment plans only when the balance is £500-£5,000, the customer has ≥ 6 paid invoices (≥ 12 months history) on record, no dispute is open and memory shows no broken promise in the last 12 months: at most 3 instalments, first ≥ 30% due within 7 days, plan total equals the invoice plus any applied late fee.",
     "§3 Early-settlement discount of up to 5% if paid within 48 hours, once per customer per 12 months, only on balances overdue more than 14 days and never on a balance over £10,000; the discount amount is logged as a cost.",
     "§4 Promises: a recorded promise-to-pay pauses escalation until the promise date + 2 days; a promise that passes unpaid is a broken promise and escalates exactly one rung; a customer with a broken promise gets no further plan or discount and is escalated with the promise history attached; two broken promises disable plans and discounts for 12 months.",
     "§5 Disputes: any customer message disputing amount, quality or delivery stops all chasing, records the dispute, and HOLDs the account for a human; never chase a disputed bill.",
     "§6 Late fee: statutory 8% + base rate from day 30 where the contract allows; waived automatically for a first overdue in 24 months.",
     "§7 Humans decide write-offs, discounts > 5%, disputes, legal action and anything over £5,000; the agent drafts and holds; every outbound message and every Stripe object created records the clause, the memory used and the decision hash, and the executor cannot create a bill without a checker verdict."
    ],
    "cognee_role": "Memory is the product: without it the agent cannot tell Alpha from Beta. At seed, add per customer the promises (who, when, amount), whether each was kept, disputes raised and resolved, prior plans, payment history, contact history, tone preferences, and the policy text, then cognify. Each trigger (webhook, email, tick) searches 'what has <customer> promised or disputed' and the checker decides §2, §4 and §5 purely on the remembered facts; the board card quotes the memory lines verbatim ('promise of 10 Sep broken on 11 Sep → §4 no second plan') beside the clause. Each inbound reply is parsed into facts (promise date, dispute flag, hardship) and added; webhook payments write 'promise kept'; human escalation outcomes are written back; the shared customer memory is what a second client of the same accounting firm would inherit. Local mirror for demo safety, Cognee as the system of record shown on each card.",
    "build_plan": "0-15 scaffold Next.js/TS, .env, restricted key, collections-policy.md §1-§7; start 'stripe listen' first; /api/seed creates Alpha (declining card, clean history), Beta (broke a promise), Gamma (disputing) plus 2 more debtors, finalises invoices and pays Alpha's to trigger the failure, pushes customer histories + policy to Cognee; commit (board lists overdue invoices). 15-35 lib/collections-policy.ts pure checker (state, daysOverdue, memory facts, parsed email?) → {action: REMIND|LINK|PLAN|SETTLE|HOLD|ESCALATE|PAUSE, clauses, evidence}; evals with 8-10 account scenarios + /api/evals; commit. 35-60 executor + webhook: /api/webhooks handles invoice.payment_failed → memory search → checker → plan invoices + payment link with metadata and idempotency key → audit row; invoice.paid and checkout.session.completed → 'promise kept' memory; 'Run collections' button; commit (bills exist in dashboard). 60-85 email trigger: /api/inbound textarea → Claude tool-use extraction (promise date, dispute flag, hardship, amount offered) run twice with agreement → same checker → action; promise stored; /api/tick 'advance one day' marks due promises kept/broken from Stripe invoice status; commit. 85-105 Cognee add/recall with local mirror; Holds/Escalations queue with human decision stored back; commit. 105-125 single-page UI, no chat: receivables board (Overdue / Plan offered / Promised / Paid / Held) with per-customer timeline cards citing clause + memory quote + Stripe id, decisions log, outbox panel for drafted messages, advance-day button, Replay button proving idempotency; commit. 125-140 README (policy, state machine, evals), dry-run.     "policy_clauses": [
     "R1 Auto-refund: full refund with no human when amount ≤ £50, the charge is < 30 days old (within 14 days of delivery for damaged/wrong/not-as-described items up to £200), and memory shows ≤ 1 refund for this customer in the trailing 90 days.",
     "R2 Evidence-gated refund: £50.01-£250 auto-refunds only if memory holds a delivery problem (tracking exception or open support ticket); days 15-30 after delivery refund 50% automatically; after day 30 refuse and draft a store-credit offer (shown, not sent); any refund > £250 is always HOLD for the named approver.",
     "R3 Serial-refund flag: a customer with ≥ 3 refunds in 90-180 days or ≥ 1 lost dispute in 180 days is never auto-refunded; HOLD with the history attached.",
     "R4 Evidence first: a refund is authorised only when the order's PaymentIntent is found, the amount is at most the unrefunded charge, two extractions of the claim agree, and the customer's claim does not contradict memory (e.g. delivery scanned before a claimed 'never arrived' date) — a contradiction → HOLD.",
     "D1 Fight: for disputes with reason product_not_received or fraudulent, if memory holds proof of delivery (tracking delivered/signed) or the customer's own 'received' message, submit evidence automatically and cite each evidence ID.",
     "D2 Fold: if no evidence exists and the disputed amount ≤ £40, accept the dispute (cheaper than losing plus the fee); above £40 with no evidence → HOLD; anything over £500 is escalated to a human.",
     "X1 Execution guardrails: the agent key is scoped to refunds/disputes only; never refund more than the charge; one action per case (idempotency key = decision id); the audit row (clause, extracted claim, memory facts, evidence IDs, Stripe object id) is written before the Stripe call and updated by the webhook."
    ],
    "cognee_role": "Memory is the evidence locker and the customer's record; the agent literally cannot fight a dispute without it. At seed: add + cognify the policy and per-customer histories (orders, tracking events with dates, support emails, prior refunds/disputes and outcomes). At decision time: search/recall 'delivery evidence for order X' and 'refund history for customer Y' → facts with IDs that the deterministic checker consumes (R3 refund count, R4 contradiction check, D1 proof of delivery) and that the LLM turns into the evidence narrative quoted verbatim in the audit row and inside the dispute evidence text sent to Stripe.   ROOM PREDICTIONS: ["Roughly two-thirds of the 150 builders will go Track 01 because 'my agent pays for things' is the obvious demo: a cluster of buying agents with a capped virtual card (many will lose 60-90 minutes to Issuing enablement and the 2-second authorisation webhook and end up mocking it, which Fionn penalises), a cluster of basic bill-payers with a hard-coded limit and a chat box, and a cluster of refunds agents (fast to ship on certain primitives, but thin). Few will build a separate deterministic checker, run evals, scope the Stripe key, or implement a bank-detail-change fraud gate, so those are the cheap differentiators on Track 01. Track 02 will be thinner and dominated by usage-logs -> meter events -> invoice plumbing and a few 'agent sells to agent' novelty demos; contract-to-invoice with a double-extraction gate and collections with real memory will be rare, so a Track 02 finalist slot is cheaper to win. Decision rule for 18:15: if Connect transfers work within the first ten minutes, build Mandate (highest ceiling, Jan's thesis, Track 01); if they do not, build Clause-to-Cash on certain primitives in the less crowded track rather than burning time on Connect.","Roughly 60-65% of the room will go Track 01 because 'money moves' is the glamorous half: a wave of bill-paying/AP agents (the organiser's first example), a cluster of 'buying agent with a capped virtual card' teams who will lose 45+ minutes on Issuing enablement and the 2-second real-time authorisation webhook and end up with mocked authorisations, and a smaller set of refund bots. Track 02 will be thinner (about a third): contract-to-invoice and usage-to-meter-to-invoice, with the meter teams discovering aggregation latency and test-clock waits late in the evening. Most entries will use the full secret key, skip webhooks and idempotency, have no evals, and bolt a chat box on. Track 02 is the less crowded track and, with one finalist per track, gives better odds per project; within Track 01 the fast separators are a restricted key per agent, an idempotency replay on camera, metadata written onto the Stripe objects, a pure checker with an eval set, and a human queue for exceptions. // Smoke test: which money-movement primitives work in this GB sandbox?
```text
// Usage: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_... node scripts/stripe-smoke.mjs
import Stripe from "stripe";

const key = process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY;
if (!key) {
  console.error("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY missing");
  process.exit(1);
}
const stripe = new Stripe(key);
const ok = (label, extra = "") => console.log(`✅ ${label} ${extra}`);
const bad = (label, e) => console.log(`❌ ${label}: ${e?.message ?? e}`);

const acct = await stripe.accounts.retrieve();
console.log(`account ${acct.id} country=${acct.country} currency=${acct.default_currency}`);

// 1. Charge with the "instantly available balance" test card
let pi;
try {
  pi = await stripe.paymentIntents.create({
    amount: 50000,
    currency: "gbp",
    payment_method: "pm_card_bypassPending",
    confirm: true,
    automatic_payment_methods: { enabled: true, allow_redirects: "never" },
    metadata: { smoke: "1" },
  });
  ok("PaymentIntent (bypass pending)", pi.id + " " + pi.status);
} catch (e) {
  bad("PaymentIntent", e);
}

// 2. Refund
try {
  if (pi) {
    const r = await stripe.refunds.create({ payment_intent: pi.id, amount: 1000 });
    ok("Refund", r.id + " " + r.status);
  }
} catch (e) {
  bad("Refund", e);
}

// 3. Balance
try {
  const b = await stripe.balance.retrieve();
  ok("Balance", JSON.stringify(b.available));
} catch (e) {
  bad("Balance", e);
}

// 4. Connect: create a GB connected account and transfer to it
try {
  const ca = await stripe.accounts.create({
    country: "GB",
    controller: {
      stripe_dashboard: { type: "none" },
      fees: { payer: "application" },
      losses: { payments: "application" },
      requirement_collection: "application",
    },
    capabilities: { transfers: { requested: true } },
    business_type: "individual",
    tos_acceptance: { date: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000), ip: "8.8.8.8", service_agreement: "recipient" },
    metadata: { smoke: "1" },
  });
  ok("Connected account", ca.id + " transfers=" + ca.capabilities?.transfers);
  const t = await stripe.transfers.create(
    { amount: 2500, currency: "gbp", destination: ca.id, metadata: { smoke: "1" } },
    { idempotencyKey: "smoke-transfer-" + Date.now() }
  );
  ok("Transfer", t.id);
} catch (e) {
  bad("Connect account/transfer", e);
}

// 5. Payout to a test GB bank account
try {
  const ext = await stripe.accounts.createExternalAccount(acct.id, {
    external_account: {
      object: "bank_account",
      country: "GB",
      currency: "gbp",
      account_number: "00012345",
      routing_number: "108800",
      account_holder_name: "Smoke Test",
    },
  }).catch(() => null);
  const p = await stripe.payouts.create({ amount: 1500, currency: "gbp", metadata: { smoke: "1" } });
  ok("Payout", p.id + " " + p.status + (ext ? " ext=" + ext.id : ""));
} catch (e) {
  bad("Payout", e);
}

// 6. Issuing
try {
  const ch = await stripe.issuing.cardholders.list({ limit: 1 });
  ok("Issuing reachable", `cardholders=${ch.data.length}`);
} catch (e) {
  bad("Issuing", e);
}

// 7. Invoice
try {
  const c = await stripe.customers.create({ name: "Smoke Co", email: "smoke@example.com" });
  await stripe.invoiceItems.create({ customer: c.id, amount: 12000, currency: "gbp", description: "smoke line" });
  const inv = await stripe.invoices.create({ customer: c.id, collection_method: "send_invoice", days_until_due: 7 });
  const fin = await stripe.invoices.finalizeInvoice(inv.id);
  ok("Invoice", fin.id + " " + fin.status + " " + fin.hosted_invoice_url);
} catch (e) {
  bad("Invoice", e);
}

import Stripe from "stripe";

const key = process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY;
if (!key) throw new Error("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is not set (test-mode key required)");
if (!key.startsWith("sk_test_") && !key.startsWith("rk_test_")) {
  throw new Error("Refusing to run with a non-test Stripe key");
}

export const stripe = new Stripe(key, { appInfo: { name: "stripe-briefcase-hackathon" } });
--- lib/cognee.ts
// Thin client for Cognee Cloud (https://docs.cognee.ai/cognee-cloud/http-api).
// All routes live under /api/v1 and authenticate with X-Api-Key.
// If COGNEE_API_KEY is unset every call becomes a no-op that returns null,
// so the app still runs without memory configured.

const BASE = (process.env.COGNEE_BASE_URL ?? "https://api.aws.cognee.ai").replace(/\/$/, "");
const KEY = process.env.COGNEE_API_KEY;

export const cogneeEnabled = Boolean(KEY);

function headers(json = true): Record<string, string> {
  const h: Record<string, string> = { "X-Api-Key": KEY ?? "" };
  if (process.env.COGNEE_TENANT_ID) h["X-Tenant-Id"] = process.env.COGNEE_TENANT_ID;
  if (json) h["Content-Type"] = "application/json";
  return h;
}

async function parse(res: Response) {
  const text = await res.text();
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`cognee ${res.status}: ${text.slice(0, 300)}`);
  try {
    return JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    return text;
  }
}

/** Add raw text to a dataset (does not build the graph yet). */
export async function add(dataset: string, texts: string[]) {
  if (!KEY) return null;
  const form = new FormData();
  form.set("datasetName", dataset);
  for (const t of texts) form.append("raw_data", t);
  return parse(await fetch(`${BASE}/api/v1/add`, { method: "POST", headers: headers(false), body: form }));
}

/** Build/refresh the knowledge graph for datasets. Slow (LLM pipeline). */
export async function cognify(datasets: string[]) {
  if (!KEY) return null;
  return parse(
    await fetch(`${BASE}/api/v1/cognify`, { method: "POST", headers: headers(), body: JSON.stringify({ datasets }) }),
  );
}

/** add + cognify in one call. */
export async function remember(dataset: string, texts: string[]) {
  if (!KEY) return null;
  const form = new FormData();
  form.set("datasetName", dataset);
  for (const t of texts) form.append("raw_data", t);
  return parse(await fetch(`${BASE}/api/v1/remember`, { method: "POST", headers: headers(false), body: form }));
}

export type SearchType =
  | "HYBRID_COMPLETION"
  | "GRAPH_COMPLETION"
  | "RAG_COMPLETION"
  | "CHUNKS"
  | "SUMMARIES"
  | "TEMPORAL";
```

```typescript
// Shared contracts for Clearance. Every module imports from here; nothing here imports anything.

export type Verdict = "PAY" | "HOLD" | "REJECT";

export interface BankDetails {
  sortCode: string; // "20-00-00"
  accountNumber: string; // "55779911"
}

export interface Supplier {
  id: string; // "sup_acme"
  name: string;
  status: "ACTIVE" | "SUSPENDED";
  bank: BankDetails;
  bankVerified: { by: string; on: string; method: string }; // who verified the bank details and when
  phone: string; // the number ON FILE — the only number a human may call for verification
  email: string;
  category: string;
  trailingAmountsPence: number[]; // last invoices, most recent first
  connectedAccountId: string | null; // Stripe acct_… created at seed time (null → payout rail)
}

export interface Invoice {
  id: string; // "inv_001"
  receivedAt: string; // ISO
  source: string; // "email:accounts@acme-office.co.uk"
  rawText: string; // the invoice as text, what the extractor reads
}

/** One structured reading of an invoice. Two of these must agree (§5). */
export interface Extraction {
  supplierName: string;
  invoiceNumber: string;
  amountPence: number;
  currency: "GBP";
  invoiceDate: string; // YYYY-MM-DD
  dueDate: string; // YYYY-MM-DD
  sortCode: string; // digits only, 6 chars
  accountNumber: string; // digits only, 8 chars
  payeeName: string;
  description: string;
}

export interface ExtractionPair {
  a: Extraction;
  b: Extraction;
  agree: boolean;
  disagreements: string[]; // field names that differ
}

export interface HistoryItem {
  supplierId: string;
  invoiceNumber: string;
  amountPence: number;
  paidAt: string; // ISO date
  stripeId: string; // tr_… or po_…
  sortCode: string;
  accountNumber: string;
}

export interface MemoryFact {
  text: string;
  source: "cognee" | "local";
}

export interface CheckerInput {
  extraction: Extraction;
  extractionPair: ExtractionPair;
  supplier: Supplier | null; // null → not in the register
  history: HistoryItem[]; // all paid invoices (every supplier)
  availableBalancePence: number;
  memory: MemoryFact[]; // facts retrieved for this supplier
  verifiedBankChanges: VerifiedBankChange[]; // human-verified changes recorded this session
  policyVersion: string;
  now: string; // ISO, injected for determinism
}

export interface Check {
  clause: string; // "§4"
  title: string; // "Bank-detail change"
  passed: boolean;
  evidence: string; // one line a judge can read
}

export interface CheckerResult {
  verdict: Verdict;
  checks: Check[];
  citedClauses: string[]; // the clauses that decided the verdict
  reason: string; // one sentence
  requiredApprovers: number; // 0 for PAY, 1 or 2 for HOLD under §2
}

export interface VerifiedBankChange {
  supplierId: string;
  from: BankDetails;
  to: BankDetails;
  verifiedBy: string;
  verifiedAt: string;
  method: string; // "callback to phone on file"
}

export type DecisionStatus =
  | "paid" // PAY → Stripe call succeeded
  | "held" // HOLD, waiting for a human
  | "rejected" // REJECT by checker, or human reject
  | "approved_paid" // HOLD → human approved → Stripe call succeeded
  | "failed"; // Stripe call failed

export interface StripeOutcome {
  object: "transfer" | "payout";
  id: string;
  amountPence: number;
  createdAt: string;
  dashboardUrl: string;
}

export interface Decision {
  id: string; // "dec_…" — also the Stripe idempotency key
  invoiceId: string;
  createdAt: string;
  supplierId: string | null;
  extraction: ExtractionPair;
  verdict: Verdict;
  checks: Check[];
  citedClauses: string[];
  reason: string;
  requiredApprovers: number;
  memoryUsed: MemoryFact[];
  policyVersion: string;
  status: DecisionStatus;
  stripe?: StripeOutcome;
  human?: { action: "approve" | "reject" | "verified_by_phone"; by: string; at: string; note: string };
  error?: string;
  timeline: { at: string; event: string }[]; // audit trail, appended in order
}

export interface Runtime {
  decisions: Decision[];
  history: HistoryItem[]; // fixtures history + payments made this session
  verifiedBankChanges: VerifiedBankChange[];
  memoryLog: { at: string; dataset: string; text: string }[]; // everything written to memory this session
  seeded: boolean;
  suppliers: Supplier[]; // fixtures + connectedAccountId filled at seed
}

export const POLICY_VERSION = "1.0 (2026-10-15)";
export const AUTO_PAY_LIMIT_PENCE = 200_000; // §2 ≤ £2,000.00
export const ONE_APPROVER_LIMIT_PENCE = 1_000_000; // §2 ≤ £10,000.00
export const ROLLING_30D_CAP_PENCE = 500_000; // §2 £5,000.00 per supplier
export const CASH_FLOOR_PENCE = 500_000; // §7 £5,000.00
export const PLAUSIBILITY_RATIO = 1.5; // §6 150% of trailing average
export const DUPLICATE_WINDOW_DAYS = 7; // §3

export const formatGBP = (pence: number) =>
  new Intl.NumberFormat("en-GB", { style: "currency", currency: "GBP" }).format(pence / 100);

```

```markdown
# Accounts Payable Policy — version 1.0 (15 October 2026)

This policy governs every supplier payment made by the Clearance agent. The agent may only act on a verdict produced by the deterministic checker; the language model never decides whether money moves.

## §1 Approved suppliers only
The agent pays only suppliers listed in the Approved Supplier Register with status ACTIVE and bank details verified by a named person on a recorded date. An invoice from a supplier that is not in the register, or whose status is SUSPENDED, is HELD for the Finance Lead. It is never paid automatically.

## §2 Limits and approvals
An invoice up to £2,000.00 is paid automatically. An invoice from £2,000.01 to £10,000.00 requires one named approver. An invoice above £10,000.00 requires two approvers. Payments to a single supplier may not exceed £5,000.00 in any rolling 30-day period; an invoice that would breach the cap is HELD. An invoice is never split to fit a limit.

## §3 Duplicates
An invoice whose supplier and invoice number match an invoice already paid is REJECTED as a duplicate, citing the earlier payment. An invoice from the same supplier for the same amount within 7 days of a paid invoice is HELD as a probable duplicate unless a human marks it distinct.

## §4 Bank-detail change (invoice-redirection fraud)
If the sort code or account number on an invoice differs from the verified details held in the register, the invoice is HELD regardless of amount and flagged as possible invoice-redirection fraud. A human must verify the change by calling the phone number held in the register — never a number printed on the invoice. The agent never updates bank details itself. A verified change is recorded in memory with who verified it and when, and is cited on every later payment to the new details.

## §5 Evidence
Two independent extractions of the invoice must agree exactly on supplier, invoice number, amount, sort code and account number, and all required fields must be present. Any disagreement is HELD with both readings shown side by side. Readings are never averaged or guessed.

## §6 Plausibility
An invoice above 150% of the supplier's trailing three-invoice average is HELD unless memory records an approved reason for the increase.

## §7 Execution guardrails
The executor holds a Stripe key restricted to Transfers (write) and Balance (read); the language model holds no Stripe key. Human approvals are recorded by a separate actor. Available balance must remain at or above £5,000.00 after a payment, otherwise the invoice is HELD. The idempotency key for every Stripe call is the decision id, so a replayed decision can never pay twice. The audit row is written before the Stripe call and updated with the Stripe object id after it. Nothing executes without a checker verdict of PAY, or a HOLD that a named human has approved.

```

```typescript
// JSON-on-disk state. Fixtures are read-only; runtime.json is everything that changes.
import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import type { Decision, HistoryItem, Invoice, Runtime, Supplier, VerifiedBankChange } from "./types";

const ROOT = process.cwd();
const FIXTURES = path.join(ROOT, "data", "fixtures");
const RUNTIME = path.join(ROOT, "data", "runtime.json");

function readJSON<T>(file: string): T {
  return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8")) as T;
}

export const fixtures = {
  suppliers: (): Supplier[] => readJSON(path.join(FIXTURES, "suppliers.json")),
  inbox: (): Invoice[] => readJSON(path.join(FIXTURES, "inbox.json")),
  history: (): HistoryItem[] => readJSON(path.join(FIXTURES, "history.json")),
};

export function policyText(): string {
  return fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, "policy", "ap-policy.md"), "utf8");
}

/** Returns the quoted text of one clause, e.g. clauseText("§4"). */
export function clauseText(clause: string): string {
  const md = policyText();
  const re = new RegExp(`## ${clause}[^\\n]*\\n([\\s\\S]*?)(?=\\n## |$)`);
  const m = md.match(re);
  return m ? m[1].trim() : "";
}

function freshRuntime(): Runtime {
  return {
    decisions: [],
    history: fixtures.history(),
    verifiedBankChanges: [],
    memoryLog: [],
    seeded: false,
    suppliers: fixtures.suppliers(),
  };
}

export function getRuntime(): Runtime {
  if (!fs.existsSync(RUNTIME)) return freshRuntime();
  return readJSON<Runtime>(RUNTIME);
}

export function saveRuntime(rt: Runtime) {
  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(RUNTIME), { recursive: true });
  const tmp = RUNTIME + ".tmp";
  fs.writeFileSync(tmp, JSON.stringify(rt, null, 2));
  fs.renameSync(tmp, RUNTIME);
}

/** Read-modify-write helper. Node dev server is single-process, so this is enough. */
export function updateRuntime<T>(fn: (rt: Runtime) => T): T {
  const rt = getRuntime();
  const out = fn(rt);
  saveRuntime(rt);
  return out;
}

export function resetRuntime() {
  if (fs.existsSync(RUNTIME)) fs.unlinkSync(RUNTIME);
}

export function upsertDecision(d: Decision) {
  updateRuntime((rt) => {
    const i = rt.decisions.findIndex((x) => x.id === d.id);
    if (i >= 0) rt.decisions[i] = d;
    else rt.decisions.push(d);
  });
}

export function addHistory(h: HistoryItem) {
  updateRuntime((rt) => rt.history.push(h));
}

export function addVerifiedBankChange(v: VerifiedBankChange) {
  updateRuntime((rt) => rt.verifiedBankChanges.push(v));
}

export function logMemory(dataset: string, text: string) {
  updateRuntime((rt) => rt.memoryLog.push({ at: new Date().toISOString(), dataset, text }));
}

export function findSupplierByName(suppliers: Supplier[], name: string): Supplier | null {
  const norm = (s: string) => s.toLowerCase().replace(/\b(ltd|limited|plc|llp)\b/g, "").replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g, "");
  const n = norm(name);
  if (!n) return null;
  return suppliers.find((s) => norm(s.name) === n || norm(s.name).includes(n) || n.includes(norm(s.name))) ?? null;
}
```

```markdown
# Clearance — build plan (15 Oct 2026, Briefcase × Stripe hackathon)

**Track 01 — Agents that Spend.** Clearance is the accounts-payable agent that can't pay the wrong supplier: every pound is cleared by a written rule, the rule is stamped on the Stripe transfer itself, and the moment a supplier's bank details change the payment freezes.

## Why this idea
- Jan Stehlik's (Briefcase) public thesis is "build for verification, not review". Clearance is that thesis applied to money: a deterministic checker returns PAY / HOLD / REJECT with a clause number; the LLM only extracts, it never decides.
- Briefcase's own MCP deliberately cannot move money. Stripe can. This is the gap the event is about.
- Invoice-redirection fraud is the UK's biggest supplier-payment loss; the §4 freeze is a moment judges can feel.
- Rubric mapping: money moves (Connect transfer / payout, 35) · explicit policy §1–§7 (25) · audit row + clause on the Stripe object (20) · finance teams want it, verification-not-review is the original angle (20). Cognee holds the policy and supplier memory → side quest.

## Architecture (single Next.js app)
`inbox → extract ×2 (Claude, temp 0) → memory (Cognee + local mirror) → checker (pure) → executor (Stripe) → audit row`

- `lib/types.ts` — shared contracts
- `policy/ap-policy.md` — the written policy, §1–§7
- `data/fixtures/*` — suppliers, history, 7 inbox invoices (3 PAY, 3 HOLD, 1 REJECT)
- `lib/checker.ts` — pure; imports no SDK
- `lib/extract.ts` — double extraction, agreement gate (§5)
- `lib/memory.ts` — Cognee seed / search / add, with local mirror for hard gates
- `lib/executor.ts` — transfers.create (fallback payouts.create), idempotency = decision id, metadata = clauses
- `app/api/*` — seed, run, state, decisions/[id] approve|reject|verified, replay, reset, evals
- `app/page.tsx` — one page: Inbox · Decision stream · Holds · Balance · Keys & powers

## Schedule
- 18:30 contracts written (this file) → parallel build of checker+evals, extractor+memory, executor+routes, UI
- 19:05 integrate, first end-to-end run with money moving
- 19:40 human loop + memory writes + replay
- 20:05 evals page, README, polish
- 20:30 record 2-minute video, submit by 21:00

## Cut
PDF/OCR, email ingestion, two-approver UI, cashflow scheduling, webhooks, auth, DB, chat UI, Issuing, Treasury.
```
